messages.author: ba35726f1825e326
messages.subject: TimeSegments2ZeroFile
parts:
Hi all

I am using the GGIR package to process data from a 24/7 accelerometry recording and implemented the TimeSegments2ZeroFile parameter to exclude certain time windows that I do not wish to include in my analysis. Although the code runs without errors, the intervals specified in the CSV file are not reflected in the results. In particular, the value of ENMO_fullRecordingMean, which is one of the main indicators of interest in my study, remains the same as when the code is run without the TimeSegments2ZeroFile parameter.

I have carefully reviewed the GGIR documentation (https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR) and followed the instructions to prepare both the CSV file and the R script. But I don't know where I could be going wrong.  I would appreciate any guidance or suggestions to resolve this issue.
Below I attach the R script and an example of ts2zero.csv file that I am using.

Example of ts2zero.csv: 

"filename","windowstart","windowend"

"COD1.gt3x",2024-11-07 15:15:00,2024-11-07 17:00:00
"COD1.gt3x",2024-11-07 21:00:00,2024-11-07 23:00:00
"COD1.gt3x",2024-11-08 16:00:00,2024-11-08 17:00:00
"COD1.gt3x",2024-11-11 10:15:00,2024-11-11 11:50:00

R script 

GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
     datadir="C:/Users/darey/analisis_studioAFI/data",
     outputdir="C:/Users/darey/analisis_studioAFI",
     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     #=====================
     # Part 2
     #=====================
     data_masking_strategy = 1,
     hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
     maxdur = 7,                 includedaycrit = 10,
     qwindow=c(0,24),
     do.imp = FALSE,
     TimeSegments2ZeroFile = "C:/Users/darey/analisis_studioAFI/ts2zero.csv",
     desiredtz = "America/Santiago",
     mvpathreshold =c(100.6),
     excludefirstlast = TRUE,
     includenightcrit = 16,
     #=====================
     # Part 3 + 4
     #=====================
     def.noc.sleep = 1,
     outliers.only = TRUE,
     criterror = 4,
     do.visual = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Part 5
     #=====================
     threshold.lig = c(45.8), threshold.mod = c(100.6),  threshold.vig = c(428.8),
     boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
     boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
     includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
     part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Visual report
     #=====================
     timewindow = c("WW"),
     visualreport=TRUE)

Best regards,

Daniel Reyes-Molina

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] TimeSegments2ZeroFile
parts:
The documentation clearly states https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#timesegments2zerofile 
part 2 uses this to set all acceleration values to zero and the non-wear classification to zero (meaning sensor worn)

I struggle to follow how could you interpret it as:
implemented the TimeSegments2ZeroFile parameter to exclude certain time windows that I do not wish to include in my analysis.

those are entirely different functionalities.

If you want to "exclude certain time windows" then make sure you use GGIR's day segment  analysis with parameter qwindow: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/TutorialDaySegmentAnalyses.html

Best, Vincent
